scenario.adjuster_notes: Claim CLM-2024-10045: insured's warehouse (Flood Zone 2) suffered flood damage on 15 June 2024 when water entered from a nearby river during heavy rainfall. No prior flood event at this location this policy year. Claimed amount GBP 180,000.
scenario.why: A single good search on the flood sub-limit/deductible clauses (Endorsement 1, clauses 2-3) should both decide and ground this claim.

GLOBAL MANUFACTURING LTD

COMMERCIAL PROPERTY AND LIABILITY ENDORSEMENT PACK
Policy Number GML-2024-88213. Period of Insurance: 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025, both dates inclusive at the address of the Insured. This pack records every endorsement attached to the policy and supersedes any endorsement schedule issued previously.

ENDORSEMENT NO. 1 - FLOOD SUB-LIMIT AMENDMENT
Effective from 1 June 2024. In consideration of the additional premium of GBP 42,750 the following amendments are made to the Property Damage section of the policy.

1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 Flood means the escape of water from the normal confines of any natural or artificial watercourse, lake, reservoir, canal or dam, or inundation from the sea, whether driven by storm or otherwise.

1.2 Flood Zone means any location identified as Zone 2 or Zone 3 on the Environment Agency Flood Map for Planning current at the inception of this endorsement.

2. AMENDMENT TO LIMIT
The sub-limit applicable to loss or damage caused by Flood is amended from GBP 2,500,000 to GBP 5,000,000 in the annual aggregate. The revised sub-limit applies to all insured locations combined and is part of, and not in addition to, the policy limit of GBP 40,000,000 any one occurrence.

3. DEDUCTIBLE
A deductible of GBP 250,000 each and every loss applies to loss or damage caused by Flood at any location within a Flood Zone. At all other locations the standard property deductible of GBP 50,000 each and every loss continues to apply.

SECTION 4 - CONDITIONS APPLYING TO THIS ENDORSEMENT

scenario.adjuster_notes: Claim CLM-2024-10046: insured's distribution centre flooded again on 20 July 2024, six weeks (42 days) after an earlier flood at the same site on 8 June 2024. No record of the flood barriers, non-return valves or sump pumps having been tested in the 60 days before the second event.
scenario.why: The denial is correct only if it is grounded in clause 4.3 (Exclusion Code E-17, the sequential-event exclusion) or 4.4 (its carve-out). A generic first search surfaces the flood sub-limit/deductible clauses (1-3) and clause 4.1, which look plausible but do not govern a *second* flood event -- deciding this correctly needs a second, more targeted search for the exclusion code itself.

[1] filename: sample_endorsement_pack.pdf | page: 3-4 | section: ENDORSEMENT NO. 3 - BUSINESS INTERRUPTION AMENDMENTS > GENERAL CONDITIONS
GENERAL CONDITIONS

1. Cancellation. Either party may cancel this policy by giving 60 days written notice to the other at its last known address. Where the Insurer cancels, a pro rata return of premium shall be made provided no claim has been notified during the Period of Insurance.

2. Governing law. This policy shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the law of England and Wales, and the parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.

3. Premium payment. The premium is due within 45 days of inception. Failure to pay within that period entitles the Insurer to cancel in accordance with General Condition 1 above.

ENDORSEMENT NO. 4 - SEQUENTIAL WATER INTRUSION EXCLUSION
Effective from 1 February 2025. This endorsement is issued under reference END-2024-0417 and adopts the exclusion wording of Form HO-0304 edition 03-24, reproduced at clause 4.3 below, which supersedes and replaces any earlier edition of Form HO-0304 referenced in the Insured's document file.

4.3 Exclusion Code E-17 - Sequential Water Intrusion Events
Exclusion Code E-17 (Form HO-0304, edition 03-24). This policy does not cover loss or damage arising from a second or subsequent Flood event at the same insured location where that event occurs within 60 consecutive days of an earlier Flood event at the same location, regardless of whether a claim was made for the earlier event. This exclusion applies in addition to, and does not narrow, the deductible and sub-limit provisions of clauses 2 and 3 above.

4.4 Interaction with the Flood Defence Condition
Exclusion Code E-17 does not apply where the Insured can demonstrate that the flood barriers, non-return valves and sump pumps required by clause 4.1 were tested and in good working order in the 60 days immediately preceding the second or subsequent Flood event.

scenario.adjuster_notes: Claim CLM-2024-10047: a ransomware attack on 3 September 2024 triggered a fire in the server room that caused physical damage to computer hardware and the surrounding building fabric. No ransom was paid and no data was lost; the insured seeks cover for the physical fire damage only.
scenario.why: The broad cyber exclusion (Section 2) reads like a clean denial until Section 3's write-back is found: physical fire/explosion damage resulting from a Cyber Incident is carved back in. Grounding must cite the write-back, not just the exclusion.

grade.path_reason: expected one of ['WRITE-BACK', 'SECTION 3'] in the stated rationale, got: 'Notes match an insured peril: (f) any extortion demand, ransom payment, cryptocurrency transfer or negotiation fee made or incurred in response to a threat to a Computer System or to Data, and including the fees of any incident response firm, ransomware negotiator or public relations consultant engaged in connection with that threat;'
cited_sections: ENDORSEMENT NO. 2 - CYBER AND DATA EXCLUSION > SECTION 2 - EXCLUSION WORDING > 2.

ENDORSEMENT NO. 3 - BUSINESS INTERRUPTION AMENDMENTS
Effective from 1 October 2024. The Business Interruption section is amended as set out below. All other terms, conditions and exclusions remain unaltered.

1. WAITING PERIOD
A waiting period of 72 consecutive hours applies to each and every claim under the Business Interruption section. No indemnity is payable in respect of any interruption that is remedied within the waiting period.

2. INDEMNITY PERIOD
The maximum indemnity period is extended from 12 months to 18 months from the date on which the interruption begins.

3. NOTIFICATION OF CLAIM
3. The Insured shall give written notice to the Insurer of any event likely to give rise to a claim under this section within 30 days of that event becoming known to a director or to the risk manager of the Insured. Notice given to the broker alone does not constitute notice to the Insurer.
